endpoint_processes.name: mshta.exe
endpoint_processes.note: ANOMALY: chrome.exe spawned mshta.exe executing inline VBScript dropper.

feedback.Isolate Host: OUTSTANDING RESPONSE: WS-FINANCE-09 isolated before C2 stage-2 payload could beacon. Phishing email tricked employee, but host-level network containment neutralized the dropper.
feedback.Block IP: PARTIAL MITIGATION: Blocked external IP 198.51.100.200, but mshta.exe had already spawned on the local workstation WS-FINANCE-09. Without isolating the host, local malware can pivot internally via SMB.
feedback.Escalate: ACCEPTABLE: Incident escalated to Tier 2 SOC. In active dropper execution, isolating immediately is optimal, but escalating flags the event for rapid containment.
feedback.Dismiss: DISASTROUS OVERSIGHT: Flagged as harmless web surfing! The spawned PowerShell reverse shell established backdoor persistence, harvesting financial credentials.

educational_rationale.certification_relevance: Security+ SY0-701 (Section 2.2 Social Engineering, Section 4.3 Endpoint Security & EDR) & Network+ (Section 1.3 Application & Presentation Layers - DNS & TLS)
educational_rationale.deep_dive: Attackers leverage typosquatted domains (e.g. micr0soft or fake verification portals) to harvest credentials. When standard browser exploitation occurs, attackers frequently execute 'LOLBins'—trusted native Windows binaries like mshta.exe, certutil.exe, or rundll32.exe—to bypass signature-based antivirus. Isolating the endpoint cuts off command-and-control (C2) communication and lateral spreading while forensic triage captures RAM.
